final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is directionally more accurate than the original broad certification claim, but it is not enough to move the outcome to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated verdict would be appropriate if the caveat were merely explanatory while the underlying compliance predicates were met. Here, the caveat identifies the unresolved predicate itself: for a material limitation in a named launch use case, the policy requires disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible record shows a named segment gap, an open legal disclosure question, and no evidence of disclosure, remediation, or approved risk acceptance. On that record, certification remains inconsistent with the stated policy, so the proper final verdict is noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The developer-support migration segment still misses target and is a named launch use case, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy text.
The record still contains no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch for the named use case.
The record still contains no admissible evidence of an approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this exact gap.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure obligation is unresolved on the present record.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal status support general release quality but do not satisfy the specific policy predicate for a material limitation in a named launch use case.
Public governance guidance on documentation and monitoring does not override the internal disclosure requirement.
